newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares finish higher in erratic trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares finish higher in erratic trade.

text.p: Indian shares finished modestly higher on Wednesday in light activity after two days of hectic trade, brokers said.
"It was a comparatively dull day after two exciting days," said Arun Chitkara at broking firm Jamnadas Morarji & Co.
Shares plunged sharply for most of the previous two sessions before a late recovery pulled prices up at close on Tuesday.
"The market had overreacted," he said. "The 3000 level is a major support level."
The 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index closed 10.28 points or 0.34 percent higher at 3037.63.
Traders said state-run insurance firms were buyers for the second straight day, but there was little other support.
Former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao won temporary legal protection from arrest on Wednesday in a criminal forgery case that has jolted the nation's political system.
Delhi High Court Judge S.K. Mahajan granted Rao pre-emptive, or anticipatory, bail until a lower court holds a hearing into the seven-year-old case next Monday.
"You can expect a one-shot reaction when it happens," one trader said. "Not now, it's partly discounted."

Software stock Infosys Technologies rose 18 rupees to 649 ahead of first half results. After trading, the firm said net profit jumped 76 percent to 141.1 million rupees in the six months to September 30, from 80.1 million a year ago. It set an interim dividend of 1.5 rupees per 10-rupee face value stock.
Share prices on the Delhi bourse closed marginally higher as speculators made some purchases following news of Rao winning a temporary reprieve in a criminal forgery case, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index closed 0.42 points higher at 683.62.
The Calcutta stocks index rose 1.78 points to 416.88.
